title: A fresh HTTP-cached catalog hides newly published lecture PDFs in the reader

source.summary: Found during actual L014 post-publication reader verification; PDF publication itself is valid.

environment.device: Mac headless browser; emulated mobile viewport
environment.display_mode: 390px browser viewport; not a physical iPad

steps: Visit L013 before deployment to warm the public manifest HTTP cache.
After L014 deployment, open its reader link in the same browser.
Compare simultaneous default and no-cache manifest requests before expiry.
observed.expected: The newly published PDF opens without clearing personal notes or storage.
observed.actual: Default reused the old167-document/13-unit catalog with max-age=600 and missed L014; no-cache immediately returned the new168-document/14-unit catalog. SW is push-only and CacheStorage was empty. Direct public PDF remained available.

limitations: Direct reproduction used isolated Firefox158, not a physical iPad/Pencil. Raw responses, headers and screenshots remain private.

policy_decision.rationale: A time-limited reader failure with direct-PDF and natural-expiry alternatives: P2. Narrow maintenance during authorized publication; no other schedules or work priorities changed.
policy_decision.revisit_when: A new lecture or PDF edition fails to open with a warm HTTP cache.

authority.basis: Existing publication authorization and Nov8 approved ADOPT maintenance.
authority.current_scope: Manifest revalidation, validated cached fallback, reader module version and regression tests. Preserve PDFs, IDs, ink, account permissions, subscriptions and authoring/mail schedules.

acceptance_criteria: Original code fails and fixed code opens the new unit with the same real600s HTTP cache.
Network/invalid-response failure preserves cached public and private PDF access.
Explicit selection during either await wins over startup restoration.
Independent candidate, continuity, all four CI jobs and actual HTTPS original flow pass; old PDFs and notes remain unchanged.
A real503/no-store revalidation must not erase the already validated in-memory catalog or existing local ink.

verification.status: Final222 reader and38 archive tests passed. Independent same-profile real HTTP-cache freshness and503 snapshot/ink/position browser checks passed; combined-source candidate and deployment pending.
checks: 217 reader tests including9 new cases passed; integrator independent rerun passed.
Counterfactual new-unit test fails on the original code.

Actual Firefox revalidation receiving503/no-store evicts the previous HTTP cache. Pre-error only-if-cached succeeds; post-error cache-only fails. Retain a validated in-memory snapshot before the fresh probe.
Final revision:222 reader tests including14 new cases passed, independently rerun by integrator. Cache-only snapshot precedes revalidation and survives HTTP503 eviction; no persistent-storage writes.
Final Firefox158: same warm600s HTTP cache old13 -> new14 conditional revalidation opens16-page L014 at page2.

Then503/no-store: a pre-captured cache-only snapshot opens the same PDF with one exact existing mouse-ink stroke and page2 retained; only one503 network request, no uncaught exception or storage clearing.
remaining_limits: Final browser, candidate and deployment verification remain pending.

next_action: ADOPT completes independent warm-cache verification, validates one candidate, deploys through existing Pages and checks the original live flow. AEDAUT lecture monitoring continues unchanged.
